001: How are you feeling after your first few weeks here at the company?
I'm adapting well, but I still find the formality of the meetings a bit strange.
That's true, here they like to follow a very strict agenda, without straying from the topic.
I noticed that too. I think I'm going to need to get used to that directness.
Over time you'll see that it actually makes our day-to-day easier.
I hope so. I'm open to learning from your culture.
002: Did you notice that the team usually has lunch together on Fridays?
I did notice. It's a very relaxed moment, different from the office atmosphere.
Exactly. Here we keep work time and social time clearly separate.
That's great. At my previous job, everything was very mixed together and exhausting.
Right, that separation helps keep productivity up without losing the human touch.
I completely agree. I'm already liking this balance more.
003: Have you already submitted the report to the board, or are you still reviewing it?
I'm still reviewing some details, because I know they really value precision.
Yes, here we can't turn in anything half-done. Reviewing is essential.
Got it. I'll put extra care into the formatting and the references before sending it.
If you need help with any part, feel free to call me, no problem.
Thank you so much. I'll take you up on that if any questions come up.
004: What did you think of yesterday's alignment meeting?
It was quite productive, but I noticed the manager didn't really like my suggestion.
Maybe he thought you don't know the internal processes well yet.
That makes sense. I'll try to understand the history of the projects better before giving my opinion.
That's a good strategy. Here, we value people who listen before they speak.
Perfect. I'll adopt that approach from now on.
005: Have you gotten used to the performance evaluation system yet?
I'm still trying to understand how the quarterly goals work.
It is confusing at first, but then you realize they're quite realistic.
Good to know. I was afraid it would be something very bureaucratic.
Don't worry. The focus here is on your development, not on punishments.
That makes me feel more at ease to keep learning.
006: Did you notice that people use a lot of technical terms in English during conversations?
I did notice. Some I know, but others still leave me lost.
Don't worry, that's normal. Over time you'll get used to the vocabulary.
Could you recommend some material for me to study those terms?
Of course! I'll send you a glossary that the company itself provides.
That will help me a lot. Thanks for your patience.
007: How are you dealing with the hierarchy here at the company?
At first I thought it would be very rigid, but the people are quite approachable.
Yes, despite the formality, the leadership is always open to dialogue.
That's a very positive point. I've had quite different experiences in the past.
Here we value mutual respect, regardless of the position.
I can see that in the day-to-day. It's a culture I really like.
008: Have you participated in any internal training since you joined?
I participated in one about nonviolent communication last week.
That's one of the team's favorites. What did you think of the content?
I found it very useful, especially for dealing with conflicts in the workplace.
They invest quite a bit in that type of training, don't they?
Definitely. It shows that the company cares about the well-being of its employees.
009: Have you gotten used to the routine of quick meetings every morning?
I admit that at first I thought they would waste a lot of time, but now I see the importance.
Right, they help align priorities and avoid rework.
Exactly. I'm already managing to organize my daily tasks better.
It's great that you're adapting so well to this pace.
It's a matter of getting used to it. I'm really enjoying it here.
010: Do you have any questions about the company's home office policies?
I do. How does the flexible schedule work on remote work days?
You can organize your routine, as long as you attend the scheduled meetings.
Understood. And is there a fixed day when everyone needs to be in the office?
Yes, Wednesdays are mandatory for the in-person alignment.
Perfect. Now everything is much clearer to me. Thanks for the explanation.
